goal: Resolve dangling wikilinks that are timestamp-identity migration scars from the RFC 0005 learning-note -> atomic-claim migration. A learning captured in session 20260514T0530 became a content-hash-slugged claim whose frontmatter carries session_id: 20260514T0530, but sibling claims still reference it in PROSE by its old identity -- either bare [[20260514T0530]] or path-form [[provenance/learning/notes/2026-05/20260514T0530-....md]]. The migration rewrote the structured frontmatter links[].to to the new entry_id but left the body wikilinks at the old timestamp identity, so they dangle. PURE PROJECTION fix in the exact mold of the just-merged G5 basename fallback: add _build_session_index to runtime/index/reindex.py (map claim frontmatter session_id -> page_id; parse frontmatter the same way _rebuild_links already does; a wiki_index or non-claim page has no session_id and is skipped), and a resolve fallback that extracts a \d{8}T\d{4} timestamp token from the wikilink basename (covers both the bare [[20260514T0530]] form and the path-form .../20260514T0530-slug.md prefix) and looks it up in the session index. Collision-safe by construction: a session_id owned by >1 claim is dropped from the index, never guessed. Tried AFTER _candidate_slugs, the entity alias_index, and the basename_index (most specific/last resort). No vault markdown is edited; only links.to_page_id is recomputed at reindex time.
